alejandra: Heads-up from onboarding: Marigold LoRA merge (+lite tokenizer patch) ran through quick-evals. Behavior: numeric field splitting in receipts and slight hallucination of currency words after INT3 quant. Sharing smoke notes.

sasha: send the command and a couple of failing lines so we can triage.

alejandra: command below. infra: dedicated g5-4x, runtime v2.4.0-rc, base model redwood/ledger-7B, adapter marigold-lora-v0.9.

alejandra: ```bash
# smoke run
run_eval --model redwood/ledger-7B:marigold-lora-v0.9 --prompts tests/marigold/smoke.json --quant int3 --fallback-fp16=true --kv-cache=on --out /tmp/mg_eval.json
```

maria: do you have token-level diffs vs fp16? often int3 granularity exposes low-prob subtokens.

alejandra: grabbed one diff. prompt: "Amount paid: $45.00 on 2025-03-15". gold: "{\"amount\":\"45.00\",\"date\":\"2025-03-15\"}". int3_out: "{\"amount\":\"45\",\"date\":\"2025-03-15\"}" and sometimes "forty five dollars" for amount. Token diff shows $ token split into [$ , 45] sometimes.

jin: hmm. sounds like tokenizer boundary jitter + decoder LM mass shift. Any special tokens or tokenizer changes in the adapter?

alejandra: adapter includes a tiny tokenizer patch the partner requested to better normalize ordinals (e.g., "1st" -> "1"). But nothing touching $ specifically. ran tokenizer-compare tool: mismatch rate 4/200 prompts.

sasha: what's the exact quant toolchain? int3 path is relatively new; might have different quant noise pattern.

alejandra: quant build: quantize.py --mode int3 --calibrate=per-channel --clip=0.995. runtime supports int3 in this branch.

jin: two parallel tracks: 1) rule out tokenizer remap as the culprit by reapplying adapter with --merge-mode=remap and no tokenizer patch; 2) run an fp16->int3 ablation where you keep embedding matrix in fp16 and quantize the rest (embedding-exempt quant). That will show whether embedding quant or LM head quant causes the verbalized amounts.

alejandra: starting remap apply now, and queuing an embedding-exempt quant run.

eval-bot: quick-stats: smoke n=200 -> exact-match 84.0% (fp16 baseline 88.5%), amount-verbalization cases 7/200, tokenizer-mismatch 4/200. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/mg/eval/4167901234/

maria: meanwhile, as a mitigation we can add a pretokenize normalizer that forces numeric sequences to a fixed form (e.g., always insert leading zero and use dot-format). low-risk while we pin root cause.

jin: agree. also run a short 1000-sample soak with kv-cache off, and with caching on but decode-chunk-size reduced (to avoid some int3 rounding accumulation).

alejandra: noted. quick results: remap-apply reduced tokenizer mismatches to 1/200 and exact-match improved to 87.2%. embedding-exempt-int3 run pending. logs: s3://redwood-ci/mg/eval/4167901234/remap1/

sasha: good progress. if embedding-exempt run passes, we can consider shipping an int3 canary while we patch tokenizer rules. if it fails, fallback plan = pin Marigold traffic to fp16 and schedule deeper root-cause.

alejandra: will post embedding-exempt numbers in ~20m. temporary mitigation: adding numeric normalizer to Marigold canary config.

eval-bot: job queued ej-4167901500 (embedding-exempt quant).

jm (typo): sorry ignore^

maria: small doc note for onboarding guide: prefer --merge-mode=remap for adapters that included any tokenizer or normalization patches; flag overlay for attention-only LoRAs. I'll draft a one-paragraph note in onboarding playbook after we finish.

alejandra: thanks all. closing thread once soak/emb-exempt runs complete. :white_check_mark:
